reason: The cited evidence (E1-E4) describes Mn dissolution, Cr retention, and Cr-rich precipitation in a Cr18Mn27Fe27.5Ni27.5 high-entropy alloy in molten FLiBe salt at 700°C. This supports the first three premises for that specific alloy and condition, but none of the evidence involves Q235 steel, aqueous harsh environments, or the 20-100°C temperature range, leaving the critical premise of applicability to Q235 steel entirely unsupported.
premises: Mn dissolution from the alloy into the environment occurs preferentially over Cr dissolution
Mn dissolution suppresses Cr dissolution into the environment
Mn dissolution leads to Cr-rich second phase precipitation
The proposed mechanism applies to Q235 steel in harsh environments at 20-100°C
